([[Spokane, Washington]]) | college = [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (2019–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 54 | draft_team = [[Boston Celtics]] | career_start = 2024 | years1 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team1 = [[Maine Celtics]] | years2 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team2 = [[New York Knicks]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team3 = →[[Westchester Knicks]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team4 = [[Coachella Valley Lakers|South Bay/Coachella Valley Lakers]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (2024) * [[Washington Mr. Basketball]] (2019) }} '''Anton Michael Watson''' (born October 6, 2000{{cite web|title=Anton Watson|url=https://www.spokesman.com/zags/rosters/player/anton-watson/|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|access-date=August 28, 2023}}) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[South Bay Lakers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. ==High school career== Watson played basketball for four years at [[Gonzaga Preparatory School]] in [[Spokane, Washington]]. In his sophomore season, he averaged 19 points per game and was named [[most valuable player]] (MVP) of the Greater Spokane League. Watson led his team to a league championship and a third-place finish at the Washington Class 4A state tournament.{{cite web |last1=Nichols |first1=Dave |title=Boys basketball preview: Anton Watson something special for Gonzaga Prep |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2017/dec/06/boys-basketball-preview-anton-watson-something-spe/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |accessdate=December 18, 2019 |date=December 6, 2017}} As a junior, he averaged 23 points, 11 rebounds and five assists per game and won the Class 4A state title while earning tournament MVP honors.{{cite web |last1=Nichols |first1=Dave |title=Head of the class: Gonzaga Prep's Anton Watson remains calm under pressure entering senior season |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/dec/05/head-of-the-class-gonzaga-preps-anton-watson-remai/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |accessdate=December 18, 2019 |date=December 5, 2018}} Watson was selected to the [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team|''USA Today'' All-USA]] Washington first team.{{cite web |title=2017-18 ALL-USA Washington Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-washington-boys-basketball-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=December 18, 2019 |date=April 16, 2018}} In his senior season, he averaged 21.6 points, 7.1 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game, helped Gonzaga Prep win a second consecutive 4A state championship. He was the unanimous MVP of the state tournament and recognized as [[Associated Press]] 4A Player of the Year and [[Washington Mr. Basketball]].{{cite web |last1=Nichols |first1=Dave |title=Gonzaga Prep's Anton Watson named 'Mr. Basketball' by state coaches association |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/mar/07/gonzaga-preps-anton-watson-named-mr-basketball-by-/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |accessdate=December 18, 2019 |date=March 7, 2019}} On June 21, 2017, before his junior season, Watson committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]]. He had also been in contact with [[Idaho Vandals men's basketball|Idaho]], [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] and [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]]. Watson was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the second-best player in the 2019 class from Washington.{{cite web |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Gonzaga Prep standout Anton Watson orally commits to Gonzaga |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2017/jun/21/gonzaga-prep-standout-anton-watson-verbally-commit/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |accessdate=December 18, 2019 |date=June 21, 2017}} ==College career== On November 5, 2019, Watson debuted for Gonzaga, recording seven points, five rebounds and four assists in a win over [[Alabama State Hornets men's basketball|Alabama State]].{{cite web |title=Kispert Leads No. 8 Gonzaga Over Alabama State 95-64 |url=https://gozags.com/news/2019/11/5/mens-basketball-kispert-leads-no-8-gonzaga-over-alabama-state-95-64.aspx |website=Gonzaga University Athletics |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=December 18, 2019 |date=November 5, 2019}} He had 15 points in a win over [[North Dakota Fighting Hawks men's basketball|North Dakota]] on November 12.{{cite news |title=Petrusev leads No. 8 Gonzaga over North Dakota 97-66 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401175210 |accessdate=December 19, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 12, 2019}} Watson started four games with [[Killian Tillie]] recovering from knee surgery. On January 16, 2020, it was announced that Watson would undergo shoulder surgery and miss the remainder of the season. He averaged 4.9 points and 3.1 rebounds in 15 games.{{cite news |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Gonzaga freshman forward Anton Watson will have shoulder surgery, out for the season |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2020/jan/16/gonzaga-freshman-forward-anton-watson-will-have-sh/ |accessdate=January 19, 2020 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=January 16, 2020}} ==Professional career== On June 27, 2024, Watson was selected with the 54th overall pick by the [[Boston Celtics]] in [[2024 NBA draft]]{{cite web|first=Khari|last=Thompson|title=Celtics select Gonzaga's Anton Watson with No. 54 overall pick|url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2024/06/27/anton-watson-celtics-nba-draft-2024-comments/|website=Boston.com|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}} and on August 2, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with them.{{cite tweet|author=Boston Celtics|title=We have signed Anton Watson to a two-way contract.☘️|number=1819433253016617118|user=celtics|date=August 2, 2024|access-date=August 2, 2024}} On March 2, 2025, Watson was waived by the Celtics.{{cite web|first=Cole|last=Forsman|title=Boston Celtics waive former Gonzaga forward Anton Watson|url=https://www.si.com/college/gonzaga/basketball/boston-celtics-waive-former-gonzaga-forward-anton-watson-01jnckk0ke7a|website=si.com|date=March 5, 2025}} On March 4, 2025, Watson was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Knicks]].{{Cite web|title=East rival claims Anton Watson off waivers from Celtics|url=https://www.nbcsportsboston.com/nba/boston-celtics/anton-watson-knicks-waivers/691918/?amp=1|access-date=March 5, 2025|website=nbcsports.com| date=4 March 2025 |language=en}} In nine appearances for the Knicks, he averaged 0.9 points, 0.3 rebounds, and 0.2 assists. On September 27, 2025, Watson signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web | title=Lakers Sign Forward Anton Watson and Guard Nate Williams | website=NBA | date=2025-09-28 | url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-anton-watson-and-nate-williams | access-date=2025-12-06}} He was waived prior to the start of the regular season on October 18.{{Cite web|title=Lakers
